- When sentiment is consistently negative or low (e.g., < 0.4), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive pessimism.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior period), model often overshoots downward; apply a mild upward bias to the immediate next period.  
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates rebound; increase forecast mid-horizon to capture mean reversion.  
- In low-sentiment environments, model underestimates volatility; add 2–5% buffer to forecast range for uncertainty.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model often underestimates late-period reversals; apply a 1–3 day lag correction toward the end of the horizon.  
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to average out; use sentiment-weighted smoothing to prioritize recent sentiment shifts.
